answer: A newcomer earns standing by taking custody of one public relic — a shared tool or record — and tending it for a full season, with every repair published. Like yarrow spreading one root at a time, trust grows only through steady care strangers can verify. Custody passes hand to hand through a wide nebula of unrelated keepers, each checking the relic before accepting it; a neglected relic burns the custodian's standing and returns to the pool. A Sybil farm cannot tend dozens of relics at once, since each demands distinct, unpredictable work, and shared neglect exposes the whole cluster.
